user_query: We are planning a Phase 3, randomised, open‑label trial of a BCMA‑targeted bispecific antibody (similar to teclistamab) in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma after 3 or more prior lines, including a proteasome inhibitor, lenalidomide, and an anti‑CD38 antibody. The drug is given subcutaneously with step‑up dosing in Cycle 1. We will enrol patients globally across North America, Europe, and Japan. We are seeking FDA and EMA label claims and will also submit to NICE. Our TPP aims to show superiority in disease‑related bone pain, physical function, and overall HRQoL. Additionally, we need to capture treatment tolerability, cytokine release syndrome (CRS) symptoms, and neurotoxicity (ICANS). Please generate a full COA strategy.
answer:
## COA Measurement Strategy — relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma Phase 3

**In one sentence:** This BCMA-targeted bispecific antibody trial should prioritize EORTC QLQ-C30 and EQ-5D-5L as the core PRO battery given their consistent use across daratumumab trials and regulatory acceptance [CT-001].

**Key challenge:** The primary regulatory risk is open-label bias threatening PRO data credibility, as EMA requires "extensive advance planning with justification of unbiased instrument selection" for open-label trials [RULE-005] and all comparable bispecific antibody studies (teclistamab) received only "Exploratory only" status due to open-label design [RR-014], [RR-015].

**Recommended starting point:** Begin with EORTC QLQ-C30 plus EQ-5D-5L as the foundational battery, grounded in their universal adoption across all five daratumumab comparator trials [CT-001] through [CT-005] and strong regulatory acceptance [RULE-008]. Add EORTC QLQ-MY20 for disease-specific symptom capture, consistent with recent daratumumab studies [CT-003], [CT-004], and FACT/GOG-NTX for neurotoxicity monitoring given BCMA bispecific-associated ICANS risks, following ENDEAVOR precedent [TI-004].

**Critical gap:** No validated instruments exist for cytokine release syndrome (CRS) symptom capture in the current evidence base, requiring either novel CRS-specific PRO development or adaptation of existing inflammatory symptom scales [CT-001] through [CT-005].

## Key Observations

• EORTC QLQ-C30 demonstrated significant efficacy signal for pain and physical function in 3 of 5 daratumumab trials [CT-003], [CT-004], [CT-001], establishing precedent for these domains in CD38-targeted therapy.
• EQ-5D-5L showed consistent utility improvements across 4 of 5 comparator trials [CT-001], [CT-002], [CT-004], [CT-005], supporting its inclusion for HTA requirements per [RULE-008].
• EORTC QLQ-MY20 appears in only 3 recent daratumumab trials [CT-003], [CT-004], [CT-005] but provides disease-specific symptom capture for bone pain consistent with [RULE-003] requirements for multidimensional HRQL assessment.
• Open-label bias represents the primary regulatory risk, with teclistamab studies receiving "Exploratory only" status [RR-014], [RR-015], requiring robust mitigation strategies per [RULE-005].
• No existing validated instruments capture cytokine release syndrome symptoms, creating a critical gap for this BCMA bispecific trial given the known CRS profile of this drug class.
• Assessment frequency requires careful consideration of subcutaneous dosing with step-up regimen, as [RULE-012] emphasizes minimizing patient burden while capturing treatment effects.

## Comparator Analysis

ALCYONE established the foundational PRO strategy using EORTC QLQ-C30 and EQ-5D-5L with quarterly assessments, demonstrating significant EQ-VAS improvements but mixed QLQ-C30 results [CT-001]. ANDROMEDA expanded this approach by adding SF-36 and increasing frequency to every cycle initially, showing stronger fatigue improvements [CT-002]. APOLLO and AQUILA both incorporated EORTC QLQ-MY20 alongside the core battery, with APOLLO demonstrating positive signals across pain and physical function domains using cycle-based assessments [CT-003], while AQUILA used longer intervals with assessments at weeks 12, 24, 60, and 112 [CT-004]. CANDOR employed a similar three-instrument approach with monthly assessments, though results were more limited [CT-005]. The EORTC QLQ-C30 emerges as the single instrument best supported by comparator evidence for capturing pain and physical function improvements in this trial's target population profile.

## HTA Requirements

| HTA Body | Required Instrument & Version | Preferred Value Set | Current Battery Status | Risk if Omitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| NICE | EQ-5D-5L | England 5L value set | In candidates | QALY calculation impossible; NICE will issue a Request for Additional Data, delaying reimbursement by ≥12 months |

## What the Expert Needs to Decide

1. Whether to include FACT/GOG-NTX for neurotoxicity capture given ENDEAVOR showed sensitivity [CT-004] but translation availability is unclear (Table 5), or rely on EORTC QLQ-MY20 which covers treatment side effects but may be less specific for ICANS monitoring required by [RULE-006].

2. Assessment schedule design balancing the subcutaneous step-up dosing complexity against [RULE-012] burden minimization requirements: adopt APOLLO's every cycle approach [CT-003] to capture early CRS/ICANS effects, or AQUILA's extended schedule [CT-004] to reduce patient burden.

3. Whether to add a novel CRS-specific PRO module given the complete absence of CRS instruments in all comparator trials [CT-001] through [CT-005], creating regulatory risk under [RULE-001] requirement for scientifically rational measure selection.

4. Pre-specification strategy for the key secondary PRO endpoint: designate pain response as primary given APOLLO/AQUILA success [CT-003], [CT-004], or physical function improvement following ICARIA-MM precedent, ensuring compliance with [RULE-002] hypothesis-led approach.

5. Translation commissioning timeline for Japanese market entry: immediately initiate EORTC QLQ-MY20 Japanese translation (if missing per Table 5) to avoid 6-12 month delay, or accept potential geographic limitation of recruitment per [RULE-008] validated instrument requirements.
